Guillermo's own take for Mon, Nov 9 (his read, quote it as his, not yours): Outflow is building. Pam Rocks read N 24 gusting 29 at 7am, up from 22 at 5am and a touch ahead of the page's 23. Pemberton is still 2 hPa above Vancouver, and Environment Canada's 4am update keeps the strong wind warning for Howe Sound, outflow 20 to 25 easing near noon.

My pick is Porteau now until about 11am, NNE 20 to 22 with waves. The tide topped out at 15.1ft at 7:16am and ebbs all morning. Check before driving: Pam Rocks 22 or more on the 8am reading, go; under 20, stay home.

EC marine forecast, Howe Sound (issued 04:00 AM PCT 09 November 2026), WARNING IN EFFECT: Today Tonight and Tuesday. Strong wind warning in effect. Wind northerly outflow 20 to 25 knots diminishing to northerly outflow 10 to 20 near noon then becoming southerly inflow 15 late this evening. Wind becoming northerly outflow 10 to 20 overnight then becoming northerly outflow 15 to 25 Tuesday morning.

EC marine forecast, Strait of Georgia (south of Nanaimo) (issued 04:00 AM PCT 09 November 2026), WARNING IN EFFECT: Today Tonight and Tuesday. Gale warning in effect. Wind east 5 to 15 knots except north 15 near the mouth of Howe Sound early this morning. Wind becoming southeast 15 to 20 early this afternoon then increasing to southeast 20 to 25 late this afternoon. Wind veering to southwest 15 to 20 late this evening then backing to southeast 15 to 25 after midnight. Wind becoming southeast 20 to 30 Tuesday afternoon except southeast 35 south of Tsawwassen Tuesday evening.
